settings_toggles.notes: Controls whether the tool automatically maintains memory/context summaries from runtime-law files and memory files. Currently ENABLED. Not a slash command despite the name.
When true, skips the permission prompt when --dangerously-skip-permissions is used. Currently DISABLED — explicit flag is still required.
Default effort level for interactive sessions. Set to 'max'. Runner profiles override this for autonomous builder invocations via --effort flag.
Permission fallback when no allow/deny/ask rule matches. 'dontAsk' = auto-approve unmatched tool calls. Governance-critical: determines what Claude can do without explicit permission.
Enables all MCP servers defined in .mcp.json for this local environment.
Explicitly enabled MCP servers from .mcp.json. Currently: filesystem only.
Explicit allow list for tool calls (e.g., Bash(python3:*), Bash(git status:*), Read(//home/openclaw/**)). Full list in .claude/settings.local.json.
Explicit deny list: blocks Read on .chief.env, .google-secrets/**, .env, .env.*, secrets/**. Hard security guardrail.
Requires explicit user confirmation for: git push, git commit, sudo, rm -rf, powershell, kill, pkill, chmod, npm, pip, pip3.

cli_flags.notes: Dynamic via runner_profiles.py PREFERRED_MODELS. quick/surgical/standard → sonnet; architect → opus. Used in builder_watcher.sh and run_polish_pass.sh invocations.
Per-session effort level. Mapped from profile tier: quick=low, surgical=medium, standard=high, architect=max. Used in builder_watcher.sh. Overrides effortLevel from settings.json.

Required for --print mode with piped stdin (see OPENCLAW_RUNTIME.md guidance and related operator lessons). Used in builder_watcher.sh and run_polish_pass.sh. Without this, all write tools are silently blocked in --print mode.
Headless execution: print response and exit. Required for all autonomous builder invocations. Must be paired with --dangerously-skip-permissions for write access.
Used as 'json' in builder_watcher.sh for cost capture (sed replaces --print with '--print --output-format json'). Default is 'text'.
Per-invocation spending cap. Values from runner_profiles: quick=0.25, surgical=0.50, standard=2.00, architect=5.00. Only works with --print.
Fallback when primary model is overloaded. Currently: haiku. Only works with --print. Used in builder_watcher.sh invoke pattern.

Minimal mode: skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads, and runtime-law auto-discovery. Sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1. NOT currently used by OpenClaw but governance-relevant — would disable tool auto-loading of adapter files.

Override permission mode for the session. OpenClaw currently uses defaultMode in settings.local.json instead of this flag directly. Governance-critical if used — bypassPermissions equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions.
Codex headless mode. invoke_pattern: setsid timeout {timeout} codex exec "$(cat {prompt_file})"
Gemini headless prompt flag. invoke_pattern: setsid timeout {timeout} gemini --prompt "$(cat {prompt_file})" --yolo --output-format text
Gemini skip-confirmations flag. Equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions for Claude. Always used in OpenClaw gemini invocations.
Ollama model invocation subcommand. invoke_pattern: setsid timeout {timeout} ollama run {model} < {prompt_file}
Aider headless prompt file. Not currently used because aider is NOT on PATH.
Aider skip-confirmations flag. Not currently used because aider is NOT on PATH.
Aider disable auto-commit flag. Not currently used because aider is NOT on PATH.

hooks.notes: Hook infrastructure available in Claude Code 2.1.91 but OpenClaw has no hooks directory and has not adopted any hooks. High governance potential: PreToolUse hooks could enforce mode verification and audit logging before tool execution. HTTP hooks (added v2.1.63) could POST tool events to OpenClaw's own approval pipeline.

Project-level settings committed to git. Contains autoDreamEnabled, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt, effortLevel.
User-global settings. Lowest priority. Overridden by project and local settings. Not inspected in this pass (path: /home/openclaw/.claude/settings.json is same as project — no separate global file).

classification_taxonomy.officially_documented_builtin: Ships with Claude Code as a documented built-in slash command. Present in all recent versions.
classification_taxonomy.bundled_slash_command: Ships with Claude Code, added in a specific release (e.g., /simplify, /batch added in v2.1.63).
classification_taxonomy.mcp_provided_command: Exposed by an MCP server. May appear as a slash command or tool in the session.
classification_taxonomy.project_custom_slash_command: Defined in .claude/commands/ directory in the project root.
classification_taxonomy.user_custom_slash_command: Defined in ~/.claude/commands/ directory (user home). In this system, identical path to project commands.
classification_taxonomy.plugin_provided_command: Exposed by an installed .claude/plugins/ plugin. None currently installed in this workspace.
classification_taxonomy.local_alias_wrapper: OpenClaw shell script or launcher that maps a mode name to a CLI invocation (e.g., run_polish_pass.sh, builder_watcher.sh).
classification_taxonomy.settings_toggle: Configuration key in settings.json or settings.local.json that controls Claude Code behavior.
classification_taxonomy.cli_flag: Command-line flag passed to a runner binary (claude, codex, gemini, aider, ollama).
classification_taxonomy.nonexistent_stale_assumption: Referenced in documentation, tasks, or planning discussions but does not actually exist as a command or flag.

open_gaps.detail: aider is registered in KNOWN_RUNNERS and runner_registry.py but 'which aider' returns nothing. Any task routed to aider will fail at launch. Drift from registry spec.
open_gaps.action: Install aider or remove from KNOWN_RUNNERS if not planned for use.

open_gaps.detail: Claude Code --help output lists CLI flags and subcommands, not in-session slash commands. Classification for built-ins is based on Anthropic documentation and changelog version comparisons, not live enumeration.
